## Trigger

## Today

`SensorPermissionUiState.resolvedState` is written by `SensorPermissionViewModel`
at `SensorPermissionViewModel.kt:26,48,68,90` (init's `null`, `onLaunch`'s
outcome, `onActionClicked`'s resolved outcome, `onResumed`'s granted case).
`SensorPermissionScreen` reads `title`/`explanation`/`actionLabel` but never
`resolvedState`; every call site that sets it already drives the actual
behaviour directly, by calling `navigator.onSensorPermissionResolved()` in
the same branch — the field duplicates that decision without ever being
read.

`WaitingForPhoneUiState.hasReceivedProfile` is written once,
`WaitingForPhoneViewModel.kt:35`, when `profileRepository.observe()` emits a
profile with a non-null `lastSyncSuccessAt`. `WaitingForPhoneScreen` reads
`title`/`explanation`/`retryLabel` but never `hasReceivedProfile`, and
nothing else in `app-wear/src/main` reads it either (confirmed in G06's
investigation of the same screen's navigation gap).

`ProfileUiState.distanceLabel` is written `ProfileViewModel.kt:201`
(`DisplayFormatter.formatDistance(profile.expectedDistanceM)`).
`ProfileScreen.kt:235` declares its own local `val distanceLabel`, built
from `PhoneStringResources.Profile.distanceLabel` — a field caption text,
homonymous but unrelated to `uiState.distanceLabel`'s formatted value; the
`TextField` itself shows `distanceFieldValue`, a plain `remember`ed string
built from `uiState.expectedDistanceM.toString()`, never the formatted
label. `ProfileUiState.pressDurationLabel` follows the identical pattern:
written `ProfileViewModel.kt:204`, shadowed by a local `val
pressDurationLabel` at `ProfileScreen.kt:259`, and the field it labels shows
`longPressFieldValue`, from `uiState.longPressMs.toString()`.

`RaceDetailUiState.raceId` is written in `RaceDetailViewModel.toUiState`
(both the null-race branch, `RaceDetailViewModel.kt:117`, and the normal
branch, `:137`). `RaceDetailScreen.kt` never reads `uiState.raceId`, and
none of `RaceDetailViewModel`'s own action methods
(`onSetAsReferenceClicked`, `onRenameConfirmed`, `onDeleteConfirmed`) read
it either — each calls `raceRepository.<action>(raceId)` using the
private constructor parameter `raceId` (`RaceDetailViewModel.kt:38`), not
`uiState.raceId`.

`SegmentRowUiState.index` is written twice in `RaceDetailViewModel.buildRow`
(`RaceDetailViewModel.kt:180,213`). `RaceDetailScreen.kt` reads
`row.name`/`row.duration`/`row.cumulative`/`row.delta`/`row.deltaTone` but
never `row.index` — `buildRow` already uses the local `index` parameter,
not the field on the state it returns, to derive `name` via
`PhoneStringResources.segmentName(index)` before the row is built.

## Expected

For every one of the six fields, nothing in its screen or its ViewModel's
own action methods has a use for it beyond what already happens without
it — each call site that sets the field also drives, in the same place,
whatever behaviour the field was meant to signal (a navigator call, an
action keyed on a value the ViewModel already holds privately, a label
already produced through another means). No field names a screen that
would plausibly start reading it: each one is dropped from its `UiState`
data class, and the write that populated it is removed from its
ViewModel.

`WaitingForPhoneUiState.hasReceivedProfile` is dropped independently of
G06's fix for the same screen: G06 adds a `WatchRaceNavigator` call at the
point `WaitingForPhoneViewModel.init` currently sets `hasReceivedProfile`
— that call does not need to read the field back from `uiState`, so the
field stays dead even after G06 lands, unless it is also removed here.
